candidate_sources.title: Onion (Allium cepa)-Black Mold | Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks
candidate_sources.snippet: Black mold of onion caused by Aspergillus niger. The fungus is first detected as a black sooty mass of spores on the neck or outer scales where injury or toppling of foliage caused an opening in the skin. Includes pathogen, symptoms, and management with storage at low temperature and humidity.

candidate_sources.title: Black mold of onion | Long Island Vegetable Health (Cornell University)
candidate_sources.snippet: Black mold of onion, caused by Aspergillus niger. Infection usually is through neck tissues as foliage dies down at maturity; infected bulbs are discolored black around the neck with affected scales shriveling. Masses of powdery black spores arranged as streaks along veins between outer dry scales.

candidate_sources.title: Black Mold in Vidalia Onions: Quick Facts | Vidalia Onion Extension News (University of Georgia)
candidate_sources.snippet: Black mold caused by Aspergillus niger. Spores are everywhere in soil and air; it poses an issue with onions when conditions are hot and humid, with optimum development at 82-93Â°F. Storing bulbs at low temperatures (35Â°F to 55Â°F) and low humidity controls black mold if bulbs are cured properly.

candidate_sources.title: Description and management of Aspergillus section Nigri causing post-harvest bulbs rot of onion | Scientific Reports
candidate_sources.snippet: Among postharvest diseases of onion, black mold rot caused by Aspergillus niger is the predominant one. Temperatures beyond 30Â°C and relative humidity of 90-100% cause severe storage losses. Management includes fungicide treatments (carbendazim, tebuconazole) and eco-friendly alternatives.

candidate_sources.title: Downy Mildew / Onion and Garlic / Agriculture: Pest Management Guidelines / UC Statewide IPM Program (UC IPM)
candidate_sources.snippet: Downy mildew of onion and garlic is caused by Peronospora destructor. Symptoms appear as pale, elongated patches on leaves with grayish-violet fuzzy growth; infected leaves become pale green then yellow and collapse. Includes management and fungicide guidelines.

candidate_sources.title: Onion (Allium cepa)-Downy Mildew | Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks
candidate_sources.snippet: Onion (Allium cepa) downy mildew caused by Peronospora destructor. Irregular foliar lesions begin pale-green and progress to yellow or brown necrotic tissue; fuzzy gray-to-violet sporangia appear on leaf surfaces during high moisture. Cultural controls and fungicide recommendations provided.

candidate_sources.title: Diagnosis and Control of Onion Diseases - Purdue Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Purdue Extension publication BP-23 describing diagnosis and control of onion diseases including downy mildew (Peronospora destructor), with symptom descriptions, disease cycle, and management options.

candidate_sources.title: Peronospora destructor - Wikipedia
candidate_sources.snippet: Peronospora destructor is an oomycete plant pathogen that affects Allium genera including onions, garlic, leeks, chives, and shallots. Downy mildew is identified by purple-brown mold in irregular patches; overwinters in crop residue and soil. Control by crop rotation and fungicides.

candidate_sources.title: Soil-Borne Diseases of Onion | CSU Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Damping-off caused by Fusarium species may appear in circular to irregular shaped areas within fields, or on individual plants between healthy appearing ones. Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cepae can infect onion seedlings, causing damping-off or delayed emergence. Damping-off, fusarium basal rot, and pink root are favored by moderate to high soil temperature, frequent cropping to onions, soil compaction, poor drainage, cultivation wounds, and low soil fertility.

candidate_sources.title: Fusarium Basal Rot / Onion and Garlic / Pest Management Guidelines / UC IPM
candidate_sources.snippet: Fusarium basal rot caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae usually occurs on scattered plants or in localized areas throughout a field with a history of this problem. The fungus can infect seedlings causing damping-off. Roots may rot off, basal plates may exhibit a gray to brown discoloration, and a white to pink fungal growth can become evident between and on scales.

candidate_sources.title: Alliums, Fusarium Basal Rot | Vegetable | UMass Amherst Center for Agriculture, Food, and the Environment
candidate_sources.snippet: Fusarium basal rot of alliums is caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae. Infection occurs through the roots and basal plate and can cause seedling damping-off as well as basal plate rot in mature bulbs, with foliar wilt and dieback of leaf tips. Management includes crop rotation, well-drained soils, resistant cultivars, and sanitation.

candidate_sources.title: Onion (Allium cepa)-Fusarium Basal Rot | Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks
candidate_sources.snippet: Fusarium basal rot of onion caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae. The pathogen infects roots and the basal plate; seedlings may damp off and mature plants show yellowing, wilting, and rotting of the basal plate with pink to white mycelium. Favored by warm soils and cultural management is emphasized.

candidate_sources.title: Iris Yellow Spot Virus | New Mexico State University
candidate_sources.snippet: Iris yellow spot virus (IYSV) is a Tospovirus spread by onion thrips (Thrips tabaci). Symptoms include straw-colored, diamond-shaped lesions on leaves and seed stalks. Includes pathogen biology, symptoms, and management recommendations for onion.

candidate_sources.title: Iris Yellow Spot / Onion and Garlic / UC Statewide IPM Program (UC IPM)
candidate_sources.snippet: Iris yellow spot, caused by Iris yellow spot virus (IYSV), produces yellow to straw-colored, diamond- or spindle-shaped lesions on onion leaves and scapes. Transmitted by onion thrips (Thrips tabaci). Pest management guidelines including monitoring, cultural and chemical control.

candidate_sources.title: Iris Yellow Spot Virus in Onions - USU Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Iris Yellow Spot Virus (IYSV) is a damaging viral disease of onion. Lesions appear as concentric oblong oval rings, light green diamond-shaped areas, and tan necrotic spots on leaves and seed stalks. Spread by onion thrips (Thrips tabaci); larvae must acquire the virus to transmit it. Management focuses on prevention, thrips control, weed control, and reducing plant stress.

candidate_sources.title: Iris yellow spot virus (Tospovirus: Bunyaviridae): from obscurity to research priority
candidate_sources.snippet: IYSV symptoms in Allium spp. are yellow- to straw-coloured, diamond-shaped lesions on leaves and flowering scapes; lesions coalesce, leading to lodging of scapes. Transmitted by Thrips tabaci and less efficiently by Frankliniella fusca. Economically important threat to onion seed and bulb crops worldwide.

candidate_sources.title: Onion Yellows Phytoplasma - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
candidate_sources.snippet: Onion yellows phytoplasma (Candidatus Phytoplasma asteris OY strain) is a causal agent of onion yellows disease, producing a wide variety of symptoms on onion and garland chrysanthemum, including virescence, yellowing, phyllody, stunting, proliferation, and witches' broom. Phytoplasmas are phloem-limited pleomorphic bacteria lacking a cell wall, mainly transmitted by leafhoppers.

candidate_sources.title: Candidatus Phytoplasma asteris (yellow disease phytoplasmas) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet on Candidatus Phytoplasma asteris (yellow disease phytoplasmas), the agent of aster yellows / onion yellows, covering host range, symptoms, distribution, vectors (leafhoppers) and management.

candidate_sources.title: Aster Yellows Phytoplasma - SDSU Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Aster yellows is caused by a phytoplasma (Candidatus Phytoplasma asteris). Yellowing and stunting symptoms are more common on grasses and onions; leaves are small, twisted and yellow. Spread by aster leafhoppers; infected plants cannot be cured and should be removed, with leafhopper and weed control to limit spread.

candidate_sources.title: Aster Yellows Phytoplasma - Plant & Pest Diagnostics (Michigan State University)
candidate_sources.snippet: Aster yellows phytoplasma (Candidatus Phytoplasma asteris) infects many hosts including onion, causing yellowing, stunting, virescence and phyllody. Transmitted by aster leafhoppers; management focuses on removing symptomatic plants, controlling leafhoppers and weed hosts.

candidate_sources.title: Purple Blotch | USU
candidate_sources.snippet: Purple blotch is a disease of onion and related crops caused by Alternaria porri. Symptoms first appear as small tan spots on leaves; lesions become sunken and rapidly expand up and down the leaf. Individual lesions 1/4"-3/4" in diameter are frequently surrounded by a band of purple tissue with a reddish or purple border and yellow halo. Yield losses can approach 25%. Fungal growth is favored by temperatures of 43-93 F with an optimum of 77 F.

candidate_sources.title: Onion (Allium cepa)-Purple Blotch | Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks
candidate_sources.snippet: Onion (Allium cepa)-Purple Blotch caused by Alternaria porri. Detailed cause, symptoms, disease cycle, and cultural and chemical control recommendations for the Pacific Northwest.

candidate_sources.title: Alternaria porri - Bugwoodwiki
candidate_sources.snippet: Alternaria porri is the fungal pathogen that causes purple blotch of onion, garlic and other Allium species. Lesions begin as small white or tan flecks and develop into elongated zonate purple lesions with concentric rings; spores form under high relative humidity (>=90%).
